extracted.intended_audience: newspaper readers interested in international affairs, diplomacy, and postwar occupation policy
extracted.subtask_description: A newspaper article covering diplomatic and military developments (Greek border fighting and UN Security Council debates), the Marshall Plan conference, and the new United States directive to the Military Governor in occupied Germany. Contains quoted policy directives and procedural details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of This Directive (objectives for U.S. in Germany)
rubrics_metrics.description: This directive . . . constitutes a statement of the objectives of your Government in Germany and of the basic policies to which your Government wishes you to give effect from the present time forward. It supersedes JCS 1067/6 and its amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The directive is to be followed by the Military Governor as the authoritative statement of U.S. aims and policy in the occupation of Germany; it frames subsequent authority, priorities and actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority of Military Government
rubrics_metrics.description: Your authority as Military Governor will be broadly construed and empowers you to take action consistent with relevant international agreements, general foreign policies of this Government and with this directive, appropriate or desirable to attain your Government’s objectives in Germany or to meet military exigencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Military Governor may take measures needed to attain U.S. objectives or address military emergencies, provided actions align with international agreements, general U.S. foreign policy, and this directive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exert effort to achieve economic unity with other zones
rubrics_metrics.description: Pending arrangements for the effective treatment of Germany as an economic and political unit, you will exert every effort to achieve economic unity with other zones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Until Allies reach agreement on unified treatment, the Military Governor must pursue policies that promote economic integration across occupation zones rather than isolated zone policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: United States policy toward Germany (overarching principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: The basic interest of the United States throughout the world is just and lasting peace. Such a peace can be achieved only if conditions of public order and prosperity are created in Europe as a whole. Europe requires the economic contributions of a stable and productive Germany as well as the necessary restraints to insure that Germany is not allowed to revive its destructive militarism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy balances rehabilitation of German economic capacity (to aid European recovery) with restraints to prevent remilitarization; forms the normative basis for occupation actions and economic decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demilitarization and disarmament (no relaxation)
rubrics_metrics.description: There [is] no relaxation of effort to complete and effectively to maintain the disarmament and demilitarization of Germany. The United States has committed itself to maintain a United States army of occupation as long as foreign occupation of Germany continues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demilitarization is a continuing priority; occupation forces may be maintained as necessary to ensure demilitarization is preserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic priorities: production of coal, food, and exports
rubrics_metrics.description: The order said the highest priority should be given to increased production of coal, food and export removals, while eliminating excess industrial capacity which has been used by Germany for the purpose of making war.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Occupation policy must prioritize immediate increases in essential production and exports to support European recovery and avoid reconstitution of wartime industrial capacity; avoid permanent limitation of legitimate industrial capacity needed for living standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on restricting Germany's industrial capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: The level of industry eventually agreed upon for Germany as a basis for reparations removals, while eliminating excess industrial capacity . . . should not permanently limit Germany’s industrial capacity. The German people . . . should not be denied the right, consistent with continued disarmament, to develop their resources for the purpose of achieving higher standards of living.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While removing wartime-capable industries is required, occupation policy must avoid permanent economic crippling; permit postwar economic development compatible with security restraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: United States political objectives in Germany
rubrics_metrics.description: It is an objective of the United States Government that there should arise in Germany as rapidly as possible a form of political organization and a manner of political life which, resting on a substantial basis of economic well‑being, will lead to tranquillity within Germany and will contribute to the spirit of peace among nations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Occupation authorities are to promote political institutions and conditions that foster democracy, tranquility, and contribute to international peace; economic and educational foundations are part of this objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect and promote democratic development; prohibit destabilizing activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Your task . . . is fundamentally that of helping to lay the economic and educational bases of a sound German democracy . . . and of prohibiting those activities which would jeopardize genuinely democratic developments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies should actively support democratic institutions and suppress activities (political, organizational, military) that would endanger democratic development; ensure measures are defined and proportionate.

rubrics_metrics.name: German self-government and federal structure
rubrics_metrics.description: You will continue to promote the development in Germany of institutions of popular self-government and the assumption of direct responsibility by German governmental agencies, assuring them legislative, judicial and executive powers... the most constructive development of German political life would be in the establishment throughout Germany of federal German states (Laender) and the formation of a central German government with limited powers and functions. All powers shall be vested in the Laender except such as are expressly delegated to the Central Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Occupation policy should devolve authority to German regional governments (Laender), build self-government capacity, and create a central government with strictly limited delegated powers; emphasize federalism over excessive centralization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain occupation forces as necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: The United States has committed itself to maintain a United States army of occupation as long as foreign occupation of Germany continues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presence of U.S. occupation forces is a policy instrument to ensure compliance with disarmament and to support stability; troop maintenance decisions follow from occupation obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting threshold noted for Security Council decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The motion lost because seven votes were needed. No negative vote was taken. The other members are {Colombia, Russia, Poland, China and France}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural detail reported for the UN Security Council: certain motions or proposals require seven affirmative votes and no negative votes from permanent members for passage; this procedural threshold shaped diplomatic outcomes reported in the article.
